notes.title: Update Notes for September 23rd 2025
notes.content:
Thanks for playing Fresh Tracks! Here's another small update addressing a few issues players have reported! 

Fixed achievements not unlocking on Steam Deck

Fixed cases where the incorrect Rhythmic would be equipped after using an encore in certain Boss Songs

Fixed boss shortcuts not appearing during certain points of progression

notes.title: Update Notes for September 3rd 2025
notes.content:
Thanks for playing Fresh Tracks! We’ve pushed a small update addressing a few issues players have reported:

Fixes & Improvements

True Ending Achievement
- Fixed an issue where the achievement for completing the true ending was not unlocking.
- For players who have already finished the game: re-loading your save file should retroactively unlock the achievement.
- We don’t believe you’ll need to re-beat the game, but due to the complexity of testing first-time unlocks vs. retroactive saves, we can’t 100% guarantee.

Shortcut Headers
- Shortcut text now correctly displays as “Shortcut” no matter which boss is skipped.
- Previously, all shortcut headers incorrectly showed “Skuld Kyng.”

Player Type Menu
- On PC, the Player Type selection screen (Traveller, Explorer, Adventurer, Champion) when starting a new game from the Main Menu, was incorrectly labeled as “Difficulty.”
- In Fresh Tracks, “Difficulty” should only refer to the marked difficulty of a Story Song: Easy, Medium, Hard, Expert, etc.
- This bug was introduced when localization was added for other languages. It has now been fixed and the menu properly says “Player Type.”

Prologue Screens
- The Version Number no longer appears on Mythic prologue screens.
- It now only displays in the Main Menu (except for Koda’s prologue, which takes place in the Main Menu and still shows it).

notes.title: Dev Update: Post-Demo Patches & Fixes
notes.content:
Did you play our demo during Steam Next Fest? Wondering what we’re cooking up for launch?

Fresh Tracks has been in development for a fewyears now, and as our first major release at the studio, we’re incredibly excited to finally get the full game into your hands. 

Since the demo was released, we’ve been reading through all your comments and reviews, watching tons of Twitch streams, and collecting all your feedback to make the full game as good as it can be for launch.

So what have we changed since the demo? Here’s a sneak peek into our development updates:


Snappier Sword Swings!
One of the most common pieces of feedback we heard from the demo was that the sword felt just a bit too slow - which made the gameplay feel slightly off from the music.

We’ve heard you loud and clear. The sword swing is now faster, to better match the rhythm and feel of the track. The goal is to make every slash feel good and in sync.

Here’s what the new sword action looks like now:



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257413/a852ec0c908d2e09b0a82a04fd7ff29daf2f73bd.gif"]


Mercy of the Mythics, a.k.a “God-mode”
We know some Story-Songs can be tough - just ask our marketing team! That’s why we’ve added Mercy of the Mythics, a new optional setting to help you push through the tricker tracks without breaking the balance.

Here’s how it works, when enabled: If you fail the same Story-Song multiple times, Mercy will kick in and boost your luck – but only for that specific song. That means you’ll start seeing more hearts and resyn drops to help you survive that song, without giving you an advantage on tracks you’re not stuck on.

Mercy provides a small nudge, just enough to help you get past the finish line and keep the story moving.  



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257413/c240abba401bc0a539c0ff88595958af6e876587.png"]


More Medium Levels
One big thing we heard from players: the jump from Easy to Hard felt steep. So we’re smoothing that curve.

We’ve added three new Medium versions of songs that previously only had Hard versions. The original Hard tracks are still there (and now slightly tougher, to keep them spicy) but the new Mediums offer a gentler ramp-up for players still building their skills.

More options, better balance, and a smoother journey from casual tapping to full-on rhythm mastery.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257413/733ad71f0ae504ea72b176e17fb069a2410b4db8.gif"]


Butt Reduction Surgery
Okay, we’ve officially shrunk the player’s hitbox, especially around the sides. Why? Due to Fresh Tracks’ first-person perspective, it's easy to get clipped by obstacles that just barely left your field of view when switching lanes.

So yes, your “butt” is officially smaller now — and it makes a big difference! Fewer frustrating lane changes and an all-around smoother ride. It’s one of those subtle tweaks that just feels better the moment you play.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257413/8b56458a4490b0df550a0eb21f82b07e117714e8.gif"]



We’re still working hard to improve Fresh Tracks even more before launch. We have more end-game work to do, more difficulty balancing, and all those nice little finishing touches. 

As always, let us know in the forums if you have any feedback or how you enjoyed the demo! You can also join our Discord to keep updated on our development and chat with the team.

And don’t forget to wishlist the game and follow, it means the world to us!

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3202950/Fresh_Tracks/"][/dynamiclink]Your friendly neighbourhood devs,
Buffalo Buffalo
